<explanation>
The MoAI-ADK project is an open-source, Python-based CLI framework that orchestrates AI agents in a SPEC-First TDD workflow. Its architecture can be broken down into the following high-level components:

1. User & CLI Layer  
   • User invokes commands (`moai-adk`, `/moai:1-plan`, `/moai:2-run`, `/moai:3-sync`) via a shell  
   • CLI module (`src/moai_adk/cli/*`) parses commands and forwards them to the Core Engine  

2. Core Engine (Mr. Alfred Orchestrator)  
   • Command Dispatcher & Context Manager (`command_helpers.py`, `context_manager.py`)  
   • Phase Executor (`phase_executor.py`): implements Plan → Run → Sync loop  
   • Integration Layer (`integration/engine.py`): interfaces with LLMs (Claude Code) and MCP servers  
   • Hook & Plugin Manager (`core/hooks/*`, `.claude/hooks/*`): pre- and post-tool hooks  

3. Agents & Skills  
   • Agents (`.claude/agents/moai/*.md` + generated via `builder-agent`) perform specialized tasks (SPEC writing, TDD, docs, quality, domain experts)  
   • Skills (`.claude/skills/moai-*` + Python skill modules) provide knowledge bases and patterns  
   • The Orchestrator dynamically loads agents/skills via the “modular system”  

4. Configuration, Memory & Specs  
   • Config files (`.moai/config/*.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `pyproject.toml`)  
   • Project memory (`.moai/memory/last-session-state.json`)  
   • SPEC docs (`.moai/specs/SPEC-*/spec.md`)  
   • Templates (`src/moai_adk/templates`, `.claude/output-styles`, `.claude/skills/*/modules`)  

5. Output & Documentation  
   • Auto-generated docs (`.moai/docs/`, README updates, architecture diagrams)  
   • Code artifacts: source (`src/moai_adk`), tests (`tests/`), hooks, scripts  

6. External Integrations  
   • LLM service (Claude via CLI or API)  
   • MCP servers (`.mcp.json`): Context7 (docs lookup), Sequential-Thinking (complex reasoning), Playwright (E2E), Figma, Nano-Banana (image gen)  
   • Git & CI/CD (GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/`)  

7. Testing & Quality  
   • Unit, integration, e2e, statusline, shell, hooks tests under `tests/`  
   • TRUST 5 quality checks automated by `manager-quality` agent  

Drawing the System Design Diagram:  
A. Identify Main Components (use distinct shapes/colors)  
   1. User & CLI (blue rectangle)  
   2. Core Engine / Mr. Alfred (green hexagon)  
      – Subcomponents: Command Parser, Phase Executor, Hook Manager, Integration Engine  
   3. Agents (orange circles) & Skills (orange hexagons)  
   4. Config & Memory (gray cylinders)  
   5. Specs & Templates (gray documents)  
   6. File System (gray folder)  
   7. External Services (purple clouds): LLM, MCP servers, GitHub  

B. Show Interactions with Directional Arrows  
   • User → CLI → Core Engine  
   • Core Engine → Agents/Skills  
   • Agents/Skills → Core Engine (results)  
   • Core Engine ↔ LLM/MCP (API calls)  
   • Core Engine → File System (read/write specs, memory, config, code, docs)  
   • Core Engine → External Git/CI for commit, PR creation  

C. Highlight Architectural Patterns  
   • Mediator (Mr. Alfred orchestrates agents)  
   • Pipeline (Plan → Run → Sync phases)  
   • Plugin/Modular (dynamic agent & skill loading)  
   • Adapter (integration layer for external LLMs & MCPs)  
   • Config-Driven (behavior controlled by JSON/YAML settings)  

D. Annotate Key Technologies  
   • Python 3.11+, Typer or Click for CLI  
   • PyTest for testing  
   • JSON/YAML for configs & specs  
   • Markdown for SPECs, Skills, Hooks  
   • LLM API (Claude Code), MCP server protocols  

Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:  
- As an open-source framework, emphasize extension points: where new agents/skills/hooks can be plugged in.  
- Show “Templates → CLI → Core Engine → Agents/Skills → File System” flow to illustrate how user input leads to spec generation, code, tests, docs.  
- Highlight the 3-phase loop (Plan, Run, Sync) as an inset or small flowchart next to the Core Engine.  

Diagram Elements Checklist:  
- Clear labels on every component  
- Directional arrows for data/control flow  
- Color coding: e.g., blue for front-end (CLI), green for core, orange for agents/skills, gray for storage, purple for external  
- Legend explaining shapes/colors  
- Group related subcomponents inside containers (e.g., “Core Engine” box)  

By following these guidelines, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate system architecture diagram that reflects MoAI-ADK’s modular, agent-orchestrated design, its integration with LLM/MCP services, and its SPEC-First TDD pipeline.
